age.evidence: 14 male and female mice were evaluated (6 to 24 wk old at the time of surgery)

sex.evidence: 14 male and female mice were evaluated (6 to 24 wk old at the time of surgery)

dosing.evidence: Experimental drugs included LSD [(+)-LSD (+)-tartrate (2:1), 0.3 mg kg -1 ], diazepam (2 mg kg -1 ), and dexmedetomidine (0.35 to 1.5 mg kg -1 ). Drugs were injected intraperitoneally with a 26-gauge needle immediately after predrug scans and prior to postdrug scans.

judge_notes: All three candidates returned zero assays. The judge agrees.

The only rodent work is widefield calcium imaging of cortical propagations in head-plated Thy1-GCaMP6s mice given LSD (study 4). Calcium imaging is a neural recording, which the rubric explicitly excludes as a behavioural assay.
No behavioural test (OFT, HTR, etc.) was run on the mice. The remaining datasets are human fMRI and self-report (MDMA, psilocybin, LSD), which fall outside the rodent scope.
Age set to 'mixed' with 42-168 days, the modal choice (2/3 candidates). This is the literal conversion of '6 to 24 wk old at the time of surgery'.
Route recorded as i.p. per the Methods text ('injected intraperitoneally'). Table 1 lists 'Cannula' for study 4 administration, which is an internal inconsistency in the paper.
Diazepam and dexmedetomidine were active controls in the imaging study. They were not given dosing entries because no behavioural experiment exists; this is consistent with all candidates.
Housing conditions are not described in this paper (details are deferred to ref. 62), so all housing fields are not_reported.
